decisions.reason: As a recent launch squarely within the firm's core upholstery range and presented on its own page, A has visible commitment behind it and management would be inclined to give it more time rather than reverse course quickly.
B is close to the established decorative textiles business, and with only a short time on the market in a growing industry, management can readily justify continuing it despite any early uncertainty.

C fits the firm's contract-oriented functional textile capabilities, was prominently presented on its own page, and therefore carries enough strategic and public commitment to encourage continued support.

Although less prominently displayed, D still builds on the firm's existing decoration offer, so management influenced by prior development effort would likely retain it and attribute any weak initial response to normal market ramp-up.
E extends the firm's known decorative fabric line and can be seen as compatible with its move toward renewable materials, which makes management more likely to persist with it after launch.
